'''Channing Thomas Frye''' (born May 17, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A [[power forward]]-[[Center (basketball)|center]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. He was selected eighth overall by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]], and was the first college senior to be selected in that draft. He also played for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Orlando Magic]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and [[Los Angeles Lakers]], winning an [[NBA Championship]] with the Cavaliers in the [[2016 NBA Finals]].

==High school career==
Raised [[Catholic Church|Catholic]], Frye attended [[St. Mary's High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|St. Mary's High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]],<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2021-08-12 |title=Five Famous Catholic School Graduates |url=https://catholiceducationarizona.org/articles/five-famous-catholic-school-graduates/#:~:text=NBA%20Basketball%20star%20Channing%20Frye,and%20was%20also%20raised%20Catholic. |access-date=2025-02-06 |website=Catholic Education Arizona |language=en-US}}</ref> where he was rated the No. 98 recruit in the nation by Hoop Scoop and the No. 13 center in the country by Fast Break Recruiting Service. As a junior in 1999–2000, he averaged 15 points, 12 rebounds, nine blocks and six assists per game for coach David Lopez as he led the team to a 26–7 record, a berth in the Class 5A state tournament semi-finals and a No. 19 national ranking by USA Today.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30700&ATCLID=208209436 | title=Channing Frye Profile | work=ArizonaWildcats.com | access-date=December 21, 2014}}</ref>

As a senior in 2000–01, Frye averaged 22 points, 15 rebounds, six blocks and three assists per game and he led St. Mary's to the 2001 Class 5A state championship with a 30–3 record. He was subsequently named Player of the Year by the Arizona Republic and the Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year while earning fourth-team Parade All-America and McDonald's All-America honors.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] in 2001–02, Frye was a key contributor for the Wildcats as he started 25 of 34 games after working his way into the starting lineup by late December and stayed there for the rest of the season. He earned Pac-10 All-Freshman team honors after averaging 9.5 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 23.9 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

As a sophomore in 2002–03, Frye was an honorable mention All-Pac-10 selection and earned Pac-10 Player of the Week honors on February 27, 2003, following a win over Arizona State. In 32 games (27 starts), he averaged 12.6 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.9 blocks in 25.4 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

As a junior in 2003–04, Frye earned first-team All-Pac-10 and USBWA All-District 9 team honors. In 30 games (all starts), he averaged 15.9 points, 7.4 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 2.1 blocks in 30.3 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

As a senior in 2004–05, Frye received the University of Arizona's Sapphire Award, which is given to the outstanding senior male student-athlete. He also earned the 2004–05 Pacific-10 Conference Sportsmanship Award. For a second consecutive year, he earned first-team All-Pac-10 and USBWA All-District 9 team honors, as well as first-team NABC All-NCAA District 15 selection. In 37 games (all starts), he averaged 15.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 2.3 blocks in 31.0 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

Frye finished his four-year career at Arizona with eight double-doubles in 12 NCAA Tournament appearances while registering 93 double-figure-point and 35 double-figure-rebound games.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===New York Knicks (2005–2007)===
[[File:Channing Frye2.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|left|Frye in 2008]]
Frye was selected with the eighth overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by his hometown the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30700&ATCLID=207974440 |title=Arizona's Channing Frye and Salim Stoudamire Selected in 2005 NBA Draft |publisher=ArizonaWildcats.com |date=July 5, 2005 |access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref> He scored a season-high 30 points twice during the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]]. On March 21, 2006, he sprained his left knee ligament in a game against the [[Toronto Raptors]] when Raptors guard [[Andre Barrett]] lost his balance and smashed his shoulder into Frye's knee, causing Frye to miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/1360/channing-frye-has-seen-the-video-is-not-mad-at-nate-robinson |title=Channing Frye has Seen the Video, is Not Mad at Nate Robinson |work=ESPN.com |date=March 25, 2006 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref>

During the 2006–07 season, power forward [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]] led the team in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] and [[field goal (basketball)|field goal percentage]], and was statistically superior to Frye in almost every category, but Knicks' head coach Isiah Thomas, until February 3, 2007, kept Frye in the starting lineup. Thomas' rationale was that Frye was a superior perimeter shooter, and his perimeter shooting would make it harder for teams to [[double team]] Knicks leading scorer [[Eddy Curry]]. On February 3, in a game against the [[Orlando Magic]], Thomas took Frye out of the starting lineup and replaced him with little-used [[Center (basketball)|center]], [[Jerome James]]. James had only appeared in 19 of the Knicks' 48 games, and averaged 2.7 points and 1.9 rebounds in those games. Thomas explained the change, saying, "I think Jerome is one of the best defensive big men in the game in terms of the center position."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20070203/NYKORL/recap.html |title=Curry Carries Knicks Past Magic |work=NBA.com |date=February 4, 2007 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> Frye was selected to the 2005–06 [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie first team]], and finished fifth in points (45) behind [[Chris Paul]] (58), [[Charlie Villanueva]] (56), [[Andrew Bogut]] (55), and [[Deron Williams]] (46).
{{clear}}

===Portland Trail Blazers (2007–2009)===

On June 28, 2007, Frye was traded, along with [[Steve Francis]], to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Zach Randolph]], [[Fred Jones (basketball)|Fred Jones]] and [[Dan Dickau]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Marc |last=Stein |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2919929 |title=Randolph heading to Knicks, Francis shipped to Blazers in draft-day trade |work=ESPN.com |date=June 29, 2007 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> Frye wore jersey No. 44 after wearing No. 7 with the Knicks, as guard [[Brandon Roy]] already wore No. 7 for the Trail Blazers. As a back-up center in 2007–08, Frye averaged 6.8 points and 4.5 rebounds per game.
[[File:Portland Trail Blazers crop.jpg|thumb|Frye (far right) with the Portland Trail Blazers in December 2008]]
In September 2008, Frye had surgery to remove bone spurs from his left ankle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3577116 |title=Frye likely to miss start of season following ankle surgery |work=ESPN.com |date=September 9, 2008 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> He went on to serve as a back-up once again in 2008–09 as he averaged a career-low 4.2 points and 2.2 rebounds per game.

===Phoenix Suns (2009–2014)===
On July 14, 2009, Frye signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] to a reported two-year, $3.8 million contract with an option on the second year.<ref name=suns>{{cite web |first=Stefan | last=Swiat |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/frye_signs_090714.html |title=Frye Returns Home to Play for Suns |work=NBA.com |date=July 14, 2009 |access-date=July 15, 2009}}</ref> In February 2010, Frye was selected to the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Three-Point Shootout]], becoming the first center invited since [[Sam Perkins]] in 1997.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coro |first=Paul |url=http://archive.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/2010/01/31/20100131spt-suns-channing-frye-three-point-contest.html |title=Suns' Channing Frye selected for 3-point shootout |publisher=Archive.azcentral.com |date=January 31, 2010 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref>

After not taking up his contract option, Frye signed a new five-year, $30 million contract with the Suns on July 8, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/frye_signs_100708.html |title=Suns Re-Sign Channing Frye |work=NBA.com |date=July 8, 2010 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref>

During the summer of 2012, Frye was screened at a regular team physical screening, and learned he had an enlarged heart via [[dilated cardiomyopathy]], forcing him to sit out the entire 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coro |first=Paul |url=http://archive.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/20120920phoenix-suns-channing-frye-enlarged-heart.html |title=Channing Frye says he'll likely to miss the upcoming season with an enlarged heart |publisher=Archive.azcentral.com |date=September 27, 2012 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> As a result, Frye filled in as a broadcaster during pre-game shows for the Suns, starting with the November 2 home game against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. To recover from his heart defect, he took up [[yoga]] and [[golf]], later on enduring more basketball related challenges like running and mid-range shooting. He was cleared to play for the Suns before the team's 2013 training camp practices began on August 30. He made his return on October 9, 2013, in the 104–98 preseason win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He made his first regular season return on October 30, 2013, in the 104–91 win over the Trail Blazers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131030/PORPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Suns 104, Blazers 91 |work=NBA.com |date=October 31, 2013 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref>

On June 23, 2014, Frye opted out of the final year of his contract with the Suns.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/channing-frye-opts-phoenix-suns-025347170--nba.html | work=Yahoo.com | title=Channing Frye opts out of Phoenix Suns' contract | access-date=September 5, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140905233227/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/channing-frye-opts-phoenix-suns-025347170--nba.html | archive-date=September 5, 2014 | date=June 23, 2014 | url-status=live}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2014–2016)===
On July 14, 2014, Frye signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] to a reported four-year, $32 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-channing-frye |title=Orlando Magic Sign Channing Frye |work=NBA.com |date=July 14, 2014 |access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11188647/channing-frye-agrees-join-orlando-magic | publisher=ESPN | title=Channing Frye, Magic agree | access-date=September 5, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720210353/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/11188647/channing-frye-agrees-join-orlando-magic | archive-date=July 20, 2014 | date=July 7, 2014 | url-status=live}}</ref> His first season with the Magic was disappointing on the court, as Frye averaged his lowest point and rebound totals per game since his final season in Portland.

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2016–2018)===

On February 18, 2016, Frye was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Jared Cunningham]] and a future second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/frye-trade-160218 |title=Cavaliers Acquire Channing Frye |work=NBA.com |date=February 18, 2016 |access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref> Acquired for his ability to stretch the floor and for his outside shooting, Frye, in just his second game as a Cavalier on February 24, hit four three-pointers and finished with 15 points off the bench in a 114–103 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/CHACLE/gameinfo.html |title=James, Irving lead Cavaliers past Hornets, 114–103 |work=NBA.com |date=February 24, 2016 |access-date=February 25, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801005938/http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/CHACLE/gameinfo.html |archive-date=August 1, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the Cavaliers' 2016 second round playoff series against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Frye helped the team go up 3–0 with 27 points on 10-of-13 shooting, including 7-of-9 from three-point range, in a Game 3 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160506/CLEATL/gameinfo.html |title=Frye leads another 3-point barrage, Cavs beat Hawks 121–108 |work=NBA.com |date=May 6, 2016 |access-date=May 6, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160505124945/http://www.nba.com/games/20160506/CLEATL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=May 5, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Cavaliers went on to sweep the Hawks and advance to the Eastern Conference Finals. There he helped the Cavaliers defeat the [[Toronto Raptors]] in six games. Frye's role in the [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] was reduced, as he played minor minutes over the first four games, before failing to appear in the following three games. Despite being down 3–1 following a Game 4 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]], the Cavaliers went on to win the series in seven games.
[[File:Channing Frye attacking the basket (15 February 2017).jpg|thumb|right|Frye as a member of the Cleveland Cavaliers in February 2017]]
On November 13, 2016, Frye scored a season-high 20 points in the Cavaliers' 100–93 win over the Charlotte Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899590 |title=James, Frye rally Cavaliers past Hornets, 100–93 |work=ESPN.com |date=November 13, 2016 |access-date=November 13, 2016}}</ref> On February 14, 2017, following the announcement that [[Kevin Love]] would be out for six weeks with an injury, Frye started in Love's place and had 21 points and 10 rebounds in a 116–108 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900237 |title=James, Cavs hold off Wiggins, Wolves, 116–108 |work=ESPN.com |date=February 14, 2017 |access-date=February 14, 2017}}</ref> Frye helped the Cavaliers go 12–1 over the first three rounds of the [[2017 NBA Playoffs|2017 playoffs]] to once again reach the NBA Finals, where they lost in five games to the Golden State.

===Los Angeles Lakers (2018)===
On February 8, 2018, the Cavaliers traded Frye, [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]] and a 2018 first-round draft pick to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Jordan Clarkson]] and [[Larry Nance Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Acquire Isaiah Thomas, Channing Frye in Trade with Cleveland|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180208lakers-acquire-thomas-frye|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2018|date=February 8, 2018}}</ref>

===Return to Cleveland (2018–2019)===
On July 19, 2018, Frye signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Channing Frye|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/frye-signing-2018|date=July 19, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 19, 2018}}</ref> On March 1, 2019, he announced that the 2018–19 season would be his last in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26114579/frye-retire-end-cavaliers-season|title=Frye to retire at end of Cavaliers' season|work=ESPN.com|date=March 1, 2019|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
On October 30, 2019, the [[NBC Sports Northwest]] announced that Frye joined their crew to co-host their new [[podcast]] program, Talkin’ Blazers Podcast.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/channing-frye-joins-nbcs-northwest-new-trail-blazers-podcast|title=Channing Frye joins NBCS Northwest for new Trail Blazers podcast!|date=October 30, 2019|website=nbcsports.com|access-date=October 30, 2019}}</ref>
Frye has also worked as a Studio Analyst for NBATV since 2020 and a fill-in Studio analyst for the NBA on TNT from 2021 to 2025. Channing Frye is also a proud supporter of the Purple Penguins of the AFF league, where his brother-in-law Sam Nelson is on the team.

==Personal life==
Frye is the son of the late Thomas Frye and the late Karen Mulzac-Frye.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/article/2016/11/25/channing-frye-death-father Cavs' Channing Frye out following death of father]</ref> Fellow NBA player and former teammate [[Tobias Harris]] is Frye's cousin.<ref>{{cite web|first=Adam |last=Zagoria |url=http://web.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20090716&content_id=5893288&vkey=45 |title=Harris impresses with summer play |publisher=Web.sny.tv |date=July 16, 2009 |access-date=November 13, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626152055/http://web.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20090716&content_id=5893288&vkey=45 |archive-date=June 26, 2015 }}</ref> His grandfather, John Mulzac, originally from [[Saint Vincent and the Grenadines]] was an [[Afro-Caribbean]] member of the [[Tuskegee Airmen]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/new-york/fdny-lt-john-mulzac-member-tuskegee-airmen-dies-91-article-1.2105404 |title=FDNY Lt. John Mulzac, member of Tuskegee Airmen, dies at 91 |newspaper=The New York Daily News |date=February 6, 2015 |access-date=November 26, 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/harris-frye-mourning-loss-grandfather/ |title=Harris, Frye Mourning Loss of Grandfather |work=NBA.com |date=January 30, 2015 |access-date=November 26, 2016 }}</ref> [[Henry Frye]], first black Chief Justice of the [[North Carolina Supreme Court]], is his granduncle, as the brother to Channing's grandfather Thomas Frye.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keech |first=Larry |date=2004-03-17 |title=FRYES TO MISS CHANCE FOR FAMILY REUINION CHANNING FRYE PLAYS IN RALEIGH TODAY, BUT HIS GREAT UNCLE, HENRY FRYE, WILL BE IN FLORIDA ON BUSINESS. |url=https://greensboro.com/fryes-to-miss-chance-for-family-reuinion-channing-frye-plays/article_c853ccb9-ebf2-58c3-98fc-fbde06bc9728.html |access-date=2025-01-02 |website=Greensboro News and Record |language=en}}</ref> 

Frye and his wife, Lauren (née Lisoski), have 4 children.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2010/04/no_longer_a_blazer_channing_fr.html|title=No longer a Blazer, Channing Frye still eats up his time in Portland|date=April 29, 2010|last=Tokito|first=Mike|work=OregonLive.com|access-date=June 30, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Nadine|last=Toren|url=http://www.arizonafoothillsmagazine.com/features/on-the-scene-with-nadine/2139-hot-valley-mamas-mrs-channing-frye.html|title=Hot Valley Mamas: Mrs. Channing Frye|publisher=ArizonaFoothillsMagazine.com|access-date=December 21, 2014}}</ref>

In 2007, Frye established ''The Channing Frye Foundation''. The foundation was founded with the goal of pointing youth in a positive and healthy direction. In 2010, Frye and his wife established ''The Frye Family Foundation'' in order to give back to the communities that are important to the Fryes, in particular, Portland, Oregon and Phoenix.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Frye Family Foundation |url=http://www.fryefamilyfoundation.org/ |work=FryeFamilyFoundation.org |access-date=December 21, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140131063520/http://www.fryefamilyfoundation.org/ |archive-date=January 31, 2014 }}</ref> Frye also sponsors a charity [[kickball]] tournament in Portland.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://recesstimesports.com/home/archives/channing-fryes-kick-for-kids-round-iii/ |title=Channing Frye's kickball tournament: Kick for Kids round III |last=Finn |first=Colleen |date=June 20, 2012 |website=RecessTimeSports.com |access-date=December 21, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706170526/http://recesstimesports.com/home/archives/channing-fryes-kick-for-kids-round-iii/ |archive-date=July 6, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2020, he launched [https://www.chosenfamilywines.com/ Chosen Family Wines] and then partnered with [[Kevin Love]], his former teammate and a close friend, along with Jacob Gray, and Chase Renton.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.chosenfamilywines.com/about/ |access-date=2023-06-10 |website=Chosen Family Wines |language=en-US}}</ref>
